title: Investment Services Compliance
summary: A ten-module programme giving compliance and risk staff at investment firms the tools to build, test and evidence compliance across the client journey and market activity.
intro: This training programme equips compliance and risk staff at investment firms, wealth managers and brokers to build and evidence compliance across the client journey, from permissions and suitability to client assets, market abuse and reporting.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give compliance and risk professionals in investment services a practical command of the conduct, client protection and market integrity obligations that shape their firm's business. Participants leave able to design and test controls, run a risk-based monitoring programme and see their firm the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: Authorisation scope and permissions, client categorisation, suitability and appropriateness, best execution, conflicts and inducements, product governance and costs and charges disclosure, client assets and money safeguarding, market abuse and surveillance, transaction reporting and record-keeping, and the compliance monitoring programme and supervisory engagement.
Intended Audience: Compliance officers, compliance analysts and risk managers at investment firms, wealth managers and brokers
Heads of business, operations and client asset teams responsible for first-line controls
Internal auditors and senior managers who oversee investment services compliance
Learning Objectives: Map the firm's activities to its permissions and identify perimeter risks
Apply client categorisation, suitability and appropriateness requirements across the client journey
Design controls for best execution, conflicts, inducements, product governance and disclosure
Implement robust client asset and client money safeguarding arrangements
Operate effective market abuse surveillance, transaction reporting and record-keeping
Build a risk-based monitoring programme and evidence compliance to supervisors
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, file reviews and practical templates, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of compliance, risk or operations in an investment firm is helpful. No prior knowledge of specific investment services rules is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)

modules.title: Authorisation Scope, Permissions and the Perimeter
modules.summary: How investment services and financial instruments are defined, how the firm's permissions shape what it may do, and how to manage perimeter and scope-creep risks.
objectives: Map the firm's services and instruments to its permissions
Identify perimeter risks from new products, channels and jurisdictions
Maintain an accurate regulatory business plan and notifications
syllabus: Investment services: execution, dealing, advice, portfolio management and custody
Financial instruments, derivatives and perimeter judgements
Scope creep, variations of permission and cross-border services
Change in control, notifications and the regulatory business plan

modules.title: Client Categorisation and Onboarding
modules.summary: How firms categorise clients, the protections each category brings, and how onboarding controls ensure categorisation and client information are accurate and kept up to date.
objectives: Apply retail, professional and eligible counterparty criteria correctly
Assess opt-up requests and the evidence needed to support them
Design onboarding controls for client information and terms of business
syllabus: Client categories and the protections attached to each
Elective professional clients: quantitative and qualitative tests
Know-your-client information, client agreements and periodic refresh
Common categorisation failures found by supervisors

modules.title: Suitability and Appropriateness
modules.summary: How to gather client information, assess suitability for advice and portfolio management, apply appropriateness tests for non-advised business, and evidence good outcomes.
objectives: Apply suitability requirements to advice and discretionary management
Apply appropriateness tests and warnings for non-advised services
Test advice quality through file reviews and outcome data
syllabus: Client objectives, risk tolerance, capacity for loss and knowledge
Suitability reports, ongoing suitability and portfolio drift
Appropriateness tests, warnings and execution-only business
Exercise: reviewing a sample of advice files

modules.title: Best Execution and Order Handling
modules.summary: How firms take all sufficient steps to obtain the best result for clients, handle and allocate orders fairly, and monitor execution quality.
objectives: Design an execution policy and venue selection process
Implement fair order handling, aggregation and allocation
Monitor execution quality and act on the results
syllabus: Execution factors, execution policy and client disclosure
Order handling, aggregation and fair allocation
Execution monitoring, transaction cost analysis and best execution committees
Payment for order flow and conflicts in order routing

modules.title: Conflicts of Interest and Inducements
modules.summary: How conflicts arise in investment services, how to identify, prevent and manage them, and how the rules on inducements and research payments apply.
objectives: Identify conflicts across the firm's business lines and group
Design a conflicts policy, register and escalation process
Apply inducement rules to fees, benefits and research
syllabus: Sources of conflict: proprietary trading, in-house products and remuneration
Conflicts policies, registers, information barriers and disclosure as a last resort
Inducements, minor non-monetary benefits and quality enhancement
Research payments, gifts and hospitality

modules.title: Product Governance and Costs and Charges Disclosure
modules.summary: Manufacturer and distributor product governance obligations, target market controls, and how to deliver clear, complete costs and charges disclosure before and after the sale.
objectives: Implement manufacturer and distributor product governance arrangements
Define and monitor the target market and distribution strategy
Produce accurate ex-ante and ex-post costs and charges disclosure
syllabus: Product approval, target market and negative target market
Distribution strategy, information exchange and product reviews
Ex-ante and ex-post costs and charges, including third-party product costs
Illustrations of the cumulative effect of costs on returns

modules.title: Client Assets and Client Money Safeguarding
modules.summary: How firms protect client assets and money through segregation, reconciliations and governance, and what happens when things go wrong or the firm fails.
objectives: Design segregation and trust arrangements for client assets and money
Operate reconciliations and resolve discrepancies promptly
Govern client asset arrangements and prepare for insolvency
syllabus: Segregation, trust status, acknowledgement letters and sub-custody
Internal and external reconciliations, shortfalls and breach reporting
Title transfer collateral, securities lending and use of client assets
Client asset oversight, audit reporting and resolution packs

modules.title: Market Abuse and Surveillance
modules.summary: The forms of market abuse, how inside information is controlled, and how to build surveillance that detects and reports suspicious orders and transactions.
objectives: Recognise insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and manipulation typologies
Control inside information through insider lists and personal account dealing
Design and calibrate trade and communications surveillance
syllabus: Inside information, insider lists, wall-crossing and personal account dealing
Manipulation typologies: spoofing, layering, ramping and cross-market abuse
Surveillance calibration, alert handling and communications monitoring
Suspicious order and transaction reports: quality and timeliness

modules.title: Transaction Reporting and Record-Keeping
modules.summary: How to deliver complete and accurate transaction reports, keep the records the authority expects, and use data quality testing to find and fix errors.
objectives: Explain transaction reporting obligations and common data fields
Implement reconciliation and data quality controls over reporting
Maintain records of orders, transactions and communications
syllabus: Reportable transactions, instrument and client identifiers
Reporting arrangements, reconciliations and data quality testing
Error identification, back-reporting and notification
Record-keeping: orders, communications, call recording and retention

modules.title: Compliance Monitoring and Supervisory Engagement
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a risk-based compliance monitoring programme, effective reporting to senior management and the board, and confident engagement with the supervisor.
objectives: Build a risk-based compliance monitoring plan
Report findings and remediation to senior management and the board
Prepare for supervisory visits, thematic reviews and information requests
syllabus: Compliance risk assessment and monitoring plan design
Testing methods, findings, remediation tracking and board reporting
Supervisory visits, thematic reviews and breach notifications
Workshop: seeing the firm the way a supervisor does

related.title: Crypto-Asset Compliance Programme
related.summary: An advanced twelve-module programme for compliance, risk and MLRO staff at crypto-asset service providers, from authorisation and custody to market abuse, AML/CFT and wind-down.

related.title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.

related.title: Governance, Risk and Compliance for Market Infrastructures
related.summary: A ten-module programme for boards, managers and control functions of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs and payment systems on meeting the PFMI in governance, risk, default management and recovery.

related.title: Payments and E-Money Compliance
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving payment and e-money firms the practical tools to meet safeguarding, fraud, financial crime and resilience expectations.

related.title: Private Markets and Private Credit for Managers
related.summary: An eight-module advanced programme giving private markets managers and service providers the tools to manage valuation, leverage, liquidity and conflicts risks and meet supervisory expectations.

related.title: Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation: International Edition
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping asset management and fund regulation through IOSCO and FSB standards, from fund regimes and delegation to liquidity, cross-border distribution, sustainability and resilience.
